questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When it is obvious you are going to turn, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: No, you do not need one.
Yes, always use one.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a stop light.

questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Other vehicles may not see your intentions. There could be other drivers nearby that you do not notice.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, it is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if it is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing can reduce crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs. The fit should be snug enough that it does not flap in the wind.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to shake them off.
Call the local police.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Let them pass.

questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. Change lanes and let them pass if you can do so safely. Speeding up will only increase danger by making them tailgate faster.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:

options.text: Fits snugly.
Is well-worn and broken in.
Is loose.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should your clothing do?

options.text: Be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Not cover your arms or legs.
Not include a jacket in warm weather.
Provide protection in a crash.

questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. The fit should be snug so it does not flap but loose enough for movement.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since they are all the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding an unfamiliar bike. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times first.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after one alcoholic drink, can you ride safely?

options.text: Yes, you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Yes, the alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
No, alcohol effects may still remain.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system, even with one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be seen while riding?

options.text: Orange
Black
Brown
Deep blue

questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible while riding. Wear bright clothing any time of day.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, what rules must you follow?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You can pass in a no-passing zone if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and only pass in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and only pass in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you do to be more visible?

options.text: Wear bright-colored clothing.
Wear dark clothing.
Ride without your headlight.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: What is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Leather gloves.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly alongside a vehicle is dangerous because the driver cannot see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.
Wear dark clothing.
Wave at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Also add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: If your footwear has laces, what should you do with them?

options.text: Tuck them in securely.
Let them hang loose.
Remove them from the footwear.
Glue them together.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your laces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?

options.text: Any gear that protects you.
The cheapest gear.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes at the same time.
Either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. They work best when used together.

questions.question: Which of the following does a street-legal motorcycle NOT need?

options.text: A headlight, taillight, and brake light.
Two mirrors.
A flag.
A horn.

questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have a headlight, taillight, and brake light; front and rear brakes; turn signals; a horn; and two mirrors.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: Your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can reach the ground while seated. You should be able to easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is typically a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black lettering show road rules, such as speed limits. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Look only at your mirrors.
Rely on your peripheral vision.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can still ride based on how you feel.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not ride.
Not worry about your riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking alcohol. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, you should pick:

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from thin materials.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and protect your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on the motorcycle. Laces should be tucked in so they don't get caught in moving parts.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle:

options.text: Is useless.
Can let the engine help slow the motorcycle.
Is illegal.
Should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let the engine help slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting can help slow your motorcycle. If you use engine braking, use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.
